Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune CROSS OF JESUS by Sir John Stainer (1840–1901). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Cross of Jesus

What is the doh of Cross of Jesus?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Cross of Jesus start on?

It starts on m (A in F major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

What words can be sung to Cross of Jesus?

Cross of Jesus is in the metre 8.7.8.7: lines of 8, 7, 8, 7 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it, such as Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Cross of Jesus in the public domain?

Yes. Sir John Stainer died in 1901; the tune was first published in 1887. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
